deviations_from_plan.plan_said: Six routes gate on access.ok alone.
deviations_from_plan.reality: Three do. analytics/metrics/[id]/{trend,preview,snapshot} gate at their first statement via requireAnalyticsV2AdminContext/Mutate (lib/metrics/platform/adminApiHelpers.ts), which resolves getAdminContextCached and returns 403 unless portalEligible. The lines the plan cited in those three are a second access resolution used only for scope dimensions, after the gate.
deviations_from_plan.significance: A C1-class false positive inside the plan that names C1 (§10.2). The same misreading would recur across W-15's ~500-route sweep.
deviations_from_plan.resolution: Gate added to the three genuinely exposed routes; the three already-gated routes covered as regression locks.

deviations_from_plan.reality: Three product paths let a principal alter its own authority, all reachable from components/adminV2/settings/access/AccessUsersConfigurationPage.tsx: role PATCH, access-scope PATCH (self-widening of department/site scope — a self-elevation vector that would defeat W-8 in advance), and remove POST (self-lockout).
deviations_from_plan.resolution: All three guarded. The plan's own exit criterion is 'any product path'.

deviations_from_plan.plan_said: Point the grid row at the existing ops.workflows.read / ops.workflows.write keys.
deviations_from_plan.reality: Those keys are seeded only into permission_keys (remote_schema.sql:731-732, inside seed_default_rbac). They are absent from permissions and permission_definitions. PUT /api/admin/rbac/grants:61-67 validates against permission_definitions, so the save would still 400 and still destroy the operator's other selections; and role_permission_grants_permissions_fkey (remote_schema.sql:6508) points at permissions, so the insert would fail at the database.
deviations_from_plan.resolution: Row removed instead. Seeding the bare keys is a migration, which wave 1 excludes. No route enforces workflows.* — the only references call it explicitly insufficient — so the row granted nothing and could only destroy input. W-10 regenerates the grid from the catalog, so the row returns once W-11 seeds an enforced workflows key.

rejected_options: b — keep the row and schedule a migration seeding workflows.read/write into permissions, permission_keys and permission_definitions
c — keep the row visible but disabled with an explanatory state
operator_decision.consequence: The W-3 remedy of record is removal, not the repoint the plan text recommends. No migration is owed. §11 remains a nine-migration register.

residual_risks: W-2 closes the self-elevation ban only. PUT /api/admin/rbac/grants still lets a caller widen their OWN role's grants — self-elevation at role level rather than membership level. That is W-18's subset rule and is D3-dependent; it is not closed here and must not be assumed shut.

W-1's declared capability is reports.read/reports.write, granted to admin for every org by 20260505164000 but NOT to ops by that migration. Today that is inert because the portalEligible leg admits ops unconditionally — but when W-13 replaces that leg with portal.access, an ops principal without reports.read would lose analytics. W-13 must re-check this route family.
The §10.3 fixture matrix (F1-F10) was not built, though §10.3 asks for it in wave 1. Waves 2-5 cannot inherit what does not exist.
W-4 (service-client principal check) is not done; the exception baseline W-15 is sized against does not yet exist.
